title: Token Chorus — cost allocation composer & export patterns
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Design and prototype a composable token-level cost analytics view ("Token Chorus") that lets product and finance users build, inspect, and export multi-dimensional cost breakdowns across models, routes, and user segments, plus a pricing-ladder UI to map token bands to ratecards. Prior work explored heatmaps and ledgers; this ticket focuses on a composer-first UX, export controls (PII-safe), and a pricing pattern editor suitable for role-based views.
background: Teams repeatedly ask for more flexible, exportable token-level analysis: ability to pivot by model variant, prompt template, customer segment, and route; to define custom price bands; and to produce auditable exports for chargeback and forecasting. Current console views are static (per-route lists or per-model sparkline) and lack composability and privacy-safe export controls. This design aims to bridge the gap between an exploratory UI and a reproducible, enterprise-ready export flow.
goals: Provide a composer UI that lets users drag-and-drop dimensions (model, route, prompt-template, user-segment) to create ad-hoc breakdowns
Expose a pricing-ladder editor so teams can define per-token price bands and preview computed chargeback across selected time windows
Offer export flows with privacy controls (anonymize IDs, redact prompt text) and multiple formats (CSV, Parquet), including schema and sample row preview
Ship a high-fidelity prototype for usability testing and gather engineering feedback for backend aggregation requirements
user_stories: As a finance analyst, I want to pivot token spend by model variant and customer team so I can produce chargeback reports
As a platform PM, I want to define a pricing ladder and preview impact on historical usage so I can propose new reserved pricing tiers
As a security reviewer, I want exports to default to anonymized user IDs and redacted text unless explicitly approved
As an engineer, I want clear acceptance criteria for required aggregation metrics and export schemas so I can scope storage and query changes
acceptance_criteria: Composer UI: Users can add up to 6 dimensions and see a stacked bar + pivot table preview updating within 250ms for 30-day sample data
Pricing ladder editor: User can create overlapping and non-overlapping token bands, assign rate per-band, and see row-level computed cost in preview

Export flow: CSV and Parquet exports include columns [date, route, model_variant, prompt_template, user_segment, tokens_prompt, tokens_response, tokens_total, computed_cost], with an option to redact prompt_template and to anonymize user IDs
Security: Default export setting is anonymize=true and redact_text=true; any export with redact_text=false must trigger an audit log and require a role flag
Prototype: High-fidelity Figma screens and interactive flows delivered; usability session notes collected from at least 4 finance/platform users
Engineering alignment: PRD and backend aggregation spec linked and acknowledged by ENG owner in comments
design_work_done: Low-fidelity sketches exploring composer grid vs column-picker patterns
High-fidelity Figma prototype (composer, pricing ladder modal, export modal, row preview and sample query) — link in attachments
Micro-interaction specs for drag-and-drop, dimension autocomplete, smart-suggested pivots, and inline cost sparklines
Accessibility pass: keyboard flows for composer, color contrast checks for stacked bars, and screen-reader labels for export toggles

review_feedback: Design review 2025-03-01: Move saved-templates CTA closer to composer header, add inline tooltip explaining 'pricing-ladder' semantics, and include sample CSV row preview adjacent to export toggles
Accessibility review 2025-03-02: Increase focus styles on drag handles and ensure export modal provides clear confirmation language about data retention and who can download

Eng review 2025-03-03: Backend requires two new endpoints: /aggregations/token-chorus/preview and /exports/token-chorus/initiate. Need contract sketch before handoff. Also requested an optional 'approximate-only' mode for very large windows
decisions: Ship composer as first-class workspace with max 6 dimensions to limit complexity
Pricing ladder will be a modal editor storing named ladders (reusable) scoped to orgs with role-based visibility
Default export settings will be anonymize=true and redact_text=true; an admin can enable raw_text_export but all events will generate audit logs in KMS-backed audit store
Prototype will use sampled production data (anonymized) for usability testing; full-scale performance testing will be separate ENG ticket
risks: Performance: naive query approach will not scale for multi-dimension pivots across 90+ day windows
Privacy: if redact controls are user-hidden, accidental exports could expose prompt content with PII
Complexity: pricing-ladder semantics (overlap rules) may confuse users without clear previews and validation

estimated_business_value: High — enables chargeback and tiered pricing discussions, reduces finance manual work, and unlocks enterprise exports
notes_for_engineering: Preview API should support 'approximate=true|false' to toggle sampled fast path
Aggregation keys: date, org_id, route, model_variant, prompt_template_hash, user_segment; token counts should be pre-rolled up at daily granularity
Export job will be asynchronous with status webhooks; include export schema v1 and sample row in PRD
